title: §17-002: End-to-End HTTP Service Testing with Supertest
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §17-002 (End-to-End HTTP Service Testing with Supertest).

cards.concept: End-to-End HTTP Service Testing with Supertest: TDD Red-Green-Refactor Lifecycle
cards.question: What is the core principle of the Refactor phase in the Test-Driven Development (TDD) Red-Green-Refactor cycle?

options.text: Adding new user features while tests are failing.
Improving code structure, removing duplication, and optimizing design while ensuring all tests continue to pass.
Deleting tests that are difficult to maintain.
Rewriting the test suite from scratch.

cards.explanation: In TDD: Red (write a failing test), Green (write minimal code to make it pass), Refactor (clean and optimize code while keeping tests green).
cards.pitfall: Skipping the Refactor phase accumulates technical debt and duplication despite having passing tests.
cards.citation: Kent Beck: Test-Driven Development by Example

cards.concept: End-to-End HTTP Service Testing with Supertest: Supertest End-to-End API Verification
cards.question: How does Supertest execute HTTP integration tests against a Node.js `http.Server` instance efficiently?

options.text: By spawning an external browser instance via Selenium.
By passing the HTTP server instance to ephemeral ephemeral ports or directly invoking internal request handlers without external network latency.
By mocking the TCP protocol stack with fake buffers.
By rewriting HTTP endpoints to GraphQL queries.

cards.explanation: Supertest binds the server to an ephemeral port (port 0) or feeds requests into the server handler, testing real routing, middleware, headers, and status codes.
cards.pitfall: Testing only 200 OK responses while neglecting to test 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, and 500 error boundary behaviors.
cards.citation: Supertest API Documentation / HTTP Testing Best Practices
